title: Which Google Cloud ETL tool fits you?

questions.hint: This one answer removes about half the list.

options.label: Keep a live database in sync with BigQuery
options.why: you want database changes copied, and Datastream is built for that, while the Data Transfer Service runs scheduled transfers

options.label: Load SaaS apps or ad data on a schedule
options.why: you need connectors for apps like Salesforce or Google Ads

options.label: Process streams or files with custom logic
options.why: you need to reshape data on the way, in code

options.label: Build pipelines visually, across tools
options.why: analysts want to click rather than code

questions.q: Who will build and run the pipelines?

options.label: Engineers who write code
options.why: Dataflow and Spark both mean writing and running code

options.label: Nobody, I want a vendor to run it
options.why: these are run by the vendor, so there are no servers for you to look after

questions.q: How do you want to pay?

options.label: By the amount of data copied
options.why: Datastream bills per GiB processed, Fivetran per active row and Hevo per event

options.label: By the hour or second of compute
options.why: these bill compute time rather than data volume

options.label: Free software that I host myself
options.why: Airbyte Core is free to self-host, and you pay for servers and staff

options.label: I want a price printed on the page
options.why: Matillion prints no dollar price for an edition or a credit

options.label: BigQuery tables
options.why: most tools here can write BigQuery

options.label: Iceberg files on Cloud Storage
options.why: the Data Transfer Service writes only BigQuery, and Fivetran and Airbyte both document Iceberg on Cloud Storage

options.label: Plain files on Cloud Storage
options.why: Datastream, Dataflow and Matillion streaming can write to Cloud Storage, and Fivetran writes Parquet there

questions.q: How much do you already have in place?

options.label: Nothing, and I want the quickest start
options.why: these are managed, so there is little to host beyond connecting a source

options.label: Spark jobs or Airflow already
options.why: you can keep running what you have

options.label: SQL models in BigQuery that need scheduling
options.why: Dataform and Composer handle SQL steps and schedules

datastream.name: Datastream
datastream.summary: Google's log-based change capture and replication from MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle and SQL Server into BigQuery, Cloud Storage or Iceberg tables.
datastream.bestWhen: you want a live copy of a database in BigQuery without running servers.
datastream.watchOut: the bill counts processed bytes that Google says can be 2 to 5 times your data, and Iceberg output is append-only.

dataflow.name: Dataflow
dataflow.summary: Google's serverless service for stream and batch jobs, with ready-made templates and Apache Beam code.
dataflow.bestWhen: your team writes code and wants one tool for streams and batches.
dataflow.watchOut: it is a processing engine, not a log reader, and the bill has many parts beyond the workers.

fusion.name: Cloud Data Fusion
fusion.summary: A visual pipeline builder on Google Cloud that runs each pipeline on a temporary Spark cluster.
fusion.bestWhen: analysts build pipelines by clicking and the instance will stay busy.
fusion.watchOut: the instance bills by the hour even when idle, and replication targets BigQuery only.

dts.name: BigQuery Data Transfer Service
dts.summary: Scheduled, managed loads into BigQuery from SaaS apps, Google products and object storage.
dts.bestWhen: you load Google Ads, Analytics, Salesforce or storage files into BigQuery.
dts.watchOut: it writes BigQuery only, and its incremental database mode is in Preview and can't sync deletes.

spark.name: Managed Service for Apache Spark
spark.summary: Google's managed Apache Spark, formerly called Dataproc, in serverless or cluster form.
spark.bestWhen: your team already writes Spark jobs.
spark.watchOut: you write all the code, and the page we read lists no connectors or change capture.

composer.name: Cloud Composer and Dataform
composer.summary: A job scheduler (Airflow) and a SQL step builder for BigQuery.
composer.bestWhen: you already have data in BigQuery and need to schedule and tidy it.
composer.watchOut: neither one moves data in from outside, and Composer bills for as long as an environment exists.

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A fully managed ELT service with a free plan and a documented Iceberg route on Google Cloud Storage.
fivetran.bestWhen: you want a vendor to run everything and your row counts are predictable.
fivetran.watchOut: billing is by monthly active rows, deletes count as paid rows, and list prices sit in a separate table.

hevo.name: Hevo
hevo.summary: A managed ELT service with posted tiers, a 14-day free trial and log-based pipelines.
hevo.bestWhen: a small team loads BigQuery and wants posted prices.
hevo.watchOut: Iceberg on Cloud Storage isn't stated in its docs, and streaming needs Hevo Sales to enable.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: A free self-hosted Core edition plus a paid cloud, with a GCS Data Lake destination for Iceberg.
airbyte.bestWhen: you want to self-host, or land Iceberg files on Google Cloud Storage.
airbyte.watchOut: database capture runs as scheduled syncs, and self-hosting means you run it.

matillion.name: Matillion
matillion.summary: A cloud ETL platform with a visual designer and push-down SQL in BigQuery.
matillion.bestWhen: analysts build pipelines visually and you work across more than one warehouse.
matillion.watchOut: no dollar price is printed, so you need a quote to budget, and streaming change capture is on Scale only.
